subject: convoyHauler
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: armoured convoy hauler guarding a sealed cargo pod.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning an armoured convoy hauler as a static model without joints, sketching a heavy truck with cab, armoured hull, sealed cargo pod on a trailer, and wheels at roughly 9m long and 2.8m wide.

Now I'm working out the chassis frame, wheel placement along four axles with tire and hub geometry, fenders, and the cab's lower body box plus an extruded tapered upper cabin profile.

Working out the windscreen geometry... placing its center in world coordinates and calculating the tilt angle so I can orient the box rotation for the sloped glass panel.

For the rest, I'm planning side window boxes with dark teal glass, a front bumper wedge with ram plate, glowing headlight boxes, a roof light bar positioned above the cab, and twin exhaust stacks mounted behind it.

Now I'm working out the cargo pod geometry: a horizontal octagonal cylinder as the sealed capsule body with tapered end caps and saddle-style cradle supports, sizing everything so it sits properly above the chassis without clipping.

I'm picking the color palette too—steel gray for the pod body, dark bands for the seal rings, magenta glow strips for accents, plus hazard stripe details on the end caps. Then I'm adding armor skirt plates along the hull sides between the wheels to flesh out the lower body.

For the rear I'm placing red glowing tail lights and considering a defensive turret, deciding to mount it near the front top of the pod with twin forward-pointing barrels rather than crowding it near the roof lightbar. I'm also planning side armor plating on the pod and fuel tanks along the chassis sides to round out the detail work.

Now I'm adding fuel tank cylinders between the axles, antennas with red-glowing tips on the cab, cyan underglow and neon trim strips, mirrors, dark door lines, and hubcaps -- using the glow helper from the kit for the illuminated parts, while making sure wheel and chassis heights line up correctly with the floor.

I'm also planning the attachment points list: a roof light bar, front grille, antenna array, pod hatch with its door normal and room dimensions, and a rear end cap for the pod sealing it off at the back with a plain rear door.

Now I'm adding more pieces -- a rear seal lock, a roof sensor array on the pod top, side cables along the chassis, bumper ram spikes, and possible gun mounts on doors and turret. I'm also settling on texture names like podShell, cabHull, chassisFrame, and skirt to keep material naming consistent.

I'm defining a helper function to build boxes with position, size, color, name, and optional rotation, then using extrusion to shape the cab hull from a 2D outline -- hood, windscreen slope, roof, and back -- extruded along the length axis with beveled edges.

Checking wheel clearance against the cab body, I realize the wheels poke through the lower cab edge, so I'm raising the cab bottom and roof height to avoid overlap.

Still placing details: windshield and side window heights, hood top, grille and headlight positions, and a front bumper box. I'll keep the chassis front extended slightly and leave minor wheel-chassis overlap since it's visually fine, then finalize with moderate length.
